mass.title: A guide to the Mass
mass.intro: The Mass has two main parts: the Liturgy of the Word, where God speaks to us in Scripture, and the Liturgy of the Eucharist, where bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ. Don't worry about getting every gesture right; follow the people around you.

parts.name: Entrance
parts.about: Everyone stands as the priest and ministers process in, usually with a song. When you enter the church, you can dip your fingers in holy water and make the Sign of the Cross, then genuflect (bend your right knee to the floor) toward the tabernacle before entering your pew.

parts.name: Greeting and Penitential Act
parts.about: The priest greets us with the Sign of the Cross. We then pause to remember our sins and ask God's mercy: "Lord, have mercy. Christ, have mercy. Lord, have mercy."

parts.name: Gloria
parts.about: A hymn of praise beginning with the angels' song at Christmas: "Glory to God in the highest." It is left out during Advent and Lent.

parts.name: Collect (Opening Prayer)
parts.about: The priest says "Let us pray" and gathers everyone's silent prayers into one. We answer "Amen."

parts.name: First Reading and Psalm
parts.about: Usually from the Old Testament. Then a psalm is sung or read, and we repeat a short response.

parts.name: Second Reading
parts.about: On Sundays, a reading from the New Testament letters, often from St. Paul.

parts.name: Gospel
parts.about: We stand to honour the words of Jesus. Before it we sing "Alleluia" (except in Lent). When the deacon or priest announces the Gospel, people trace a small cross on their forehead, lips and heart, asking that God's word be in our mind, on our lips and in our heart.

parts.name: Homily
parts.about: The priest or deacon explains the readings and how to live them.

parts.name: Creed
parts.about: We profess our faith together, usually with the Nicene Creed. Everyone bows at the words about Jesus becoming man.

parts.name: Prayer of the Faithful
parts.about: Prayers for the Church, the world, people in need and the local community. We usually answer "Lord, hear our prayer." In many parishes, people in RCIA are sent out with their catechists after the homily to reflect on the readings together.

parts.name: Preparation of the Gifts
parts.about: Bread and wine are brought to the altar, and the collection is taken. We stand when the priest says "Pray, brethren..."

parts.name: Eucharistic Prayer
parts.about: The heart of the Mass. After the "Holy, Holy, Holy," we kneel, as is the custom in Canada. The priest repeats Jesus' words from the Last Supper, and the bread and wine become the Body and Blood of Christ. Bells may ring as the priest lifts the Host and the chalice. It ends with a great "Amen."

parts.name: Our Father and Sign of Peace
parts.about: We pray the Lord's Prayer together, then offer each other a sign of peace, usually a handshake or a nod with "Peace be with you."

parts.name: Lamb of God
parts.about: We sing "Lamb of God, you take away the sins of the world." In many Canadian parishes we then kneel; in some, everyone stays standing until all have received. Then we say: "Lord, I am not worthy that you should enter under my roof, but only say the word and my soul shall be healed."

parts.name: Communion
parts.about: Catholics who are ready go forward to receive. Before you can receive, you can stay in your pew and pray, or go up with arms crossed over your chest to receive a blessing. Afterward, people kneel or sit in quiet prayer.

parts.name: Blessing and Dismissal
parts.about: The priest blesses us and sends us out: "Go in peace." We answer "Thanks be to God." It is good to stay for the closing song.

mass.note: These follow the Roman Missal for Canada and common practice in Canadian parishes. Each bishop can set some local customs, so postures can differ a little from one diocese to another.

basics.title: First-week basics
basics.intro: Small things that can feel confusing at first. Nobody expects you to know them yet.

items.name: Holy water
items.about: At the church door there is a font of blessed water. Dip your fingers and make the Sign of the Cross. It reminds us of our baptism. If you are not baptized yet, you are still welcome to do this.

items.name: Genuflecting
items.about: Before entering your pew, bend your right knee to the floor toward the tabernacle, the box where the consecrated Hosts are kept, usually marked by a lit candle. It is a sign of reverence to Jesus present there. If you can't kneel, a bow is fine.

items.name: The tabernacle and its candle
items.about: The red or white candle near the tabernacle is always lit when Jesus is present in the Eucharist inside. That is why Catholics keep quiet and reverent in church even before Mass.

items.name: Sign of the Cross
items.about: Touch your forehead (Father), chest (Son), left shoulder and right shoulder (Holy Spirit). Catholics in the West go left to right.

items.name: At Communion before you can receive
items.about: Stay in your pew and pray, or go up with arms crossed over your chest to receive a blessing. Both are completely normal.

items.name: Fasting before Communion
items.about: Once you can receive, Catholics fast from food and drink (except water and medicine) for one hour before Communion.

items.name: Sunday obligation
items.about: Catholics go to Mass every Sunday (or Saturday evening) and on certain holy days. Starting this habit now is one of the best ways to prepare.

items.name: What to call people
items.about: A priest is usually "Father," a deacon "Deacon," a religious sister "Sister," and the bishop "Bishop" or "Your Excellency."

items.name: What to bring and wear
items.about: Nothing is required. Dress respectfully, as you would for something important. Many parishes have the readings in a missal in the pew.

items.name: Silence
items.about: Before and after Mass, people pray quietly. Save conversations for outside the church or the gathering space.

confession.title: A guide to confession
confession.intro: In the sacrament of Reconciliation, also called confession, God forgives our sins through the priest. Nothing you say can ever be repeated by the priest. People often feel nervous the first time, and priests are used to helping. You will usually make your first confession before Easter, or after baptism if you are being baptized (baptism itself washes away all sins).

steps.name: Prepare
steps.about: Spend some quiet time with an examination of conscience (below). Ask the Holy Spirit to help you see honestly and without fear.

steps.name: Go in
steps.about: You can kneel behind a screen or sit face to face. Make the Sign of the Cross and say: "Bless me, Father, for I have sinned. This is my first confession" (or "It has been ... since my last confession").

steps.name: Confess
steps.about: Tell your sins simply, especially serious ones, and roughly how often. If you're unsure what to say, tell the priest; he will help you.

steps.name: Listen
steps.about: The priest may give some advice and a penance: a prayer or an action to do afterward.

steps.name: Say you're sorry
steps.about: Pray an Act of Contrition, from the prayer library or in your own words.

steps.name: Absolution
steps.about: The priest says the words of absolution, ending "I absolve you from your sins, in the name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Spirit." Make the Sign of the Cross and answer "Amen."

steps.name: Go in peace
steps.about: Thank God and do your penance soon. You are forgiven.

examination.heading: Loving God
questions: Have I made time for God in prayer?
Have I put anything (money, work, pleasure, approval) above God?
Have I used God's name carelessly or in anger?
Have I missed Mass on Sundays without a serious reason?

examination.heading: Loving others
questions: Have I honoured and cared for my parents and family?
Have I hurt anyone by violence, anger or harsh words? Have I held on to hatred?
Have I been faithful and pure in my thoughts, words and relationships?
Have I stolen, cheated, or been careless with what belongs to others?
Have I lied, gossiped, or damaged someone's reputation?
Have I been jealous or envious of others?

examination.heading: Myself
questions: Have I cared for my body and my health, and avoided abuse of alcohol or drugs?
Have I been lazy in my duties at home, school or work?
Have I ignored people in need when I could have helped?

rosary.title: Pray the Rosary
rosary.intro: The Rosary is a meditation on the life of Jesus, prayed with Mary. While praying the Hail Marys, you think about one event (a "mystery") from the Gospels. A full Rosary takes about 20 minutes. You don't need beads; this guide counts for you.
howto: Make the Sign of the Cross and pray the Apostles' Creed on the crucifix.
Pray an Our Father, three Hail Marys (for faith, hope and love) and a Glory Be.
For each of the five mysteries: read the scene, then pray an Our Father, ten Hail Marys while picturing it, a Glory Be and the Fatima Prayer.
Close with the Hail, Holy Queen and the Prayer After the Rosary.
Short on time? Pray just one decade. Open "The five mysteries" and choose one.

joyful.name: Joyful Mysteries
items: The Finding of Jesus in the Temple

details.verse: And Mary said: Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it done to me according to thy word.
details.reflect: The angel Gabriel asks Mary to become the mother of God's Son. She is young and does not understand everything, but she trusts God and says yes. In that yes, God becomes one of us.
details.scene: Mary saying yes to God's plan.

details.verse: Blessed art thou among women, and blessed is the fruit of thy womb.
details.reflect: Mary hurries to help her older cousin Elizabeth, who is also expecting a child. Elizabeth and the baby in her womb, John, leap for joy, because Jesus is near. Mary answers with a song of praise, the Magnificat.
details.scene: Mary going to serve Elizabeth, carrying Jesus with her.

details.verse: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him up in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.
details.reflect: The Son of God is born in a stable in Bethlehem, poor and small. The first to come and worship him are shepherds, simple workers. God comes close to us not in power but as a baby we can hold.
details.scene: The baby Jesus in the manger, with Mary and Joseph.

details.verse: Because my eyes have seen thy salvation, which thou hast prepared before the face of all peoples: a light to the revelation of the Gentiles, and the glory of thy people Israel.
details.reflect: Mary and Joseph bring baby Jesus to the Temple, as the Law asks, to offer him to God. Old Simeon and Anna, who had waited all their lives, recognize him as the Saviour. Simeon also tells Mary that a sword will pierce her heart.
details.scene: Simeon holding Jesus in his arms in the Temple.

details.verse: And he said to them: How is it that you sought me? did you not know, that I must be about my father's business?
details.reflect: When Jesus is twelve, he stays behind in Jerusalem. Mary and Joseph search for him for three days, worried, and find him in the Temple, listening and asking questions. Even when we feel we have lost Jesus, we can always find him again.
details.scene: Mary and Joseph finding Jesus in the Temple.

details.verse: Father, if thou wilt, remove this chalice from me: but yet not my will, but thine be done.
details.reflect: In the Garden of Gethsemane, Jesus prays alone while his friends fall asleep. He is afraid and in anguish, yet he gives himself to the Father's will. When we are afraid, we can pray as he did.
details.scene: Jesus praying alone in the garden at night.

details.verse: But he was wounded for our iniquities, he was bruised for our sins: the chastisement of our peace was upon him, and by his bruises we are healed.
details.reflect: Pilate has Jesus whipped by the soldiers. Jesus suffers this in silence, for us. His wounds become the place where our own wounds can be healed.
details.scene: Jesus tied to the pillar, suffering in silence.

details.verse: And platting a crown of thorns, they put it upon his head, and a reed in his right hand. And bowing the knee before him, they mocked him, saying: Hail, king of the Jews.
details.reflect: The soldiers mock Jesus with a crown of thorns and a purple cloak. He is truly a King, but his kingdom is love, not force. He bears insults patiently and does not strike back.
details.scene: Jesus crowned with thorns and mocked.

details.verse: And bearing his own cross, he went forth to that place which is called Calvary, but in Hebrew Golgotha.
details.reflect: Weak and wounded, Jesus carries his cross through the streets. He falls, and Simon of Cyrene is made to help him. When our own burdens are heavy, Jesus walks with us, and we can help carry the burdens of others.
details.scene: Jesus carrying the cross, with Simon helping.

details.verse: And Jesus said: Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
details.reflect: Jesus is nailed to the cross and dies for the sins of the world. Even then he forgives his executioners and gives his mother to us. This is the greatest act of love there has ever been.
details.scene: Jesus on the cross, with Mary and John below.

glorious.name: Glorious Mysteries
items: The Descent of the Holy Spirit

details.verse: He is not here, for he is risen, as he said. Come, and see the place where the Lord was laid.
details.reflect: On the third day the women find the tomb empty. Jesus is alive, risen in his body, and death has lost its power. This is the heart of our faith and the joy of every Easter.
details.scene: The empty tomb on Easter morning.

details.verse: This Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, shall so come, as you have seen him going into heaven.
details.reflect: Forty days after Easter, Jesus blesses his disciples and returns to the Father. He goes ahead of us to prepare a place for us, and he sends his friends out to tell the whole world.
details.scene: Jesus rising into heaven, blessing his friends.

details.verse: And they were all filled with the Holy Ghost, and they began to speak with divers tongues, according as the Holy Ghost gave them to speak.
details.reflect: Mary and the apostles are praying together when the Holy Spirit comes like wind and tongues of fire. The frightened disciples become bold witnesses. You will receive this same Spirit in Confirmation.
details.fruit: Love of God and the gifts of the Spirit
details.scene: The Holy Spirit as tongues of fire over Mary and the apostles.

details.verse: For behold from henceforth all generations shall call me blessed. Because he that is mighty, hath done great things to me; and holy is his name.
details.reflect: At the end of her life on earth, Mary was taken up body and soul into heaven. The Bible does not describe this; it is the faith the Church has held from early times (Catechism 966). What God did for Mary is what he promises to all who love him.
details.scene: Mary taken up into heaven.

details.verse: And a great sign appeared in heaven: A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet, and on her head a crown of twelve stars.
details.reflect: In heaven, Mary is honoured as Queen, because her Son is King. She is not far away: as a mother she prays for each of us. We ask her to help us stay close to Jesus all our lives.
details.scene: Mary crowned as Queen of heaven and earth.

details.verse: And behold a voice from heaven, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
details.reflect: Jesus, who has no sin, goes down into the Jordan River to be baptized by John. The heavens open, the Spirit comes down like a dove, and the Father speaks. At your own Baptism, God will say this to you too: you are my beloved child.
details.scene: The Spirit coming down on Jesus in the Jordan River.

details.verse: His mother saith to the waiters: Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.
details.reflect: At a wedding in Cana the wine runs out. Mary notices and tells Jesus, then tells the servants to do whatever he says. Jesus turns water into wine, his first sign. Mary still brings our needs to her Son.
details.scene: Mary telling the servants: do whatever he tells you.

details.verse: The time is accomplished, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent, and believe the gospel.
details.reflect: Jesus travels through Galilee announcing good news: God's kingdom is near. He heals the sick, forgives sinners and welcomes the poor. He invites each of us to turn back to God and trust him.
details.scene: Jesus preaching, healing and forgiving.

details.verse: And lo, a voice out of the cloud, saying: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased: hear ye him.
details.reflect: On a high mountain, Jesus' face shines like the sun before Peter, James and John. Moses and Elijah appear with him. The Father tells the disciples to listen to his Son, preparing them for the hard days of the cross.
details.scene: Jesus shining with light on the mountain.

details.verse: This is my body, which is given for you. Do this for a commemoration of me.
details.reflect: At the Last Supper, the night before he dies, Jesus takes bread and wine and gives them to his friends as his own Body and Blood. He gives himself to us at every Mass. At the end of RCIA you will receive him for the first time.
details.scene: Jesus giving the bread and the cup at the Last Supper.
